```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Same made-up Nebraska data as last week. Still not real.
# rio imports the data and tidyverse does the data work.
pacman::p_load(rio, tidyverse)
```

# Read in the data

```{r}
# Data is read from the R Study Group folder.
# If your EDV drive letter is different than K: you will need to change it.
linelist <- import("K:/R Study Group/Trenton/Ch12 Pivot/pivot_demo_data.xlsx")

head(linelist)
```

# group_by and summarise

```{r}
# group_by does nothing visible by itself. It just tells R how to split the rows.
# summarise then boils each group down to one row.
# n() counts the rows in the group. mean() averages a column.
# NOTE: 50 rows turn into 8, one per LHD. The counts are last week's wide table with Female + Male added together.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd) %>%
  summarise(cases = n(), mean_age = round(mean(age)))
```

```{r}
# You can group by more than one column. One row per LHD and sex.
# NOTE: same 15 rows as last week's count(lhd, sex), just with more columns.
# FYI summarise peels off the last grouping column (sex) but leaves lhd grouped. More on that at the end.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd, sex) %>%
  summarise(cases = n(), mean_age = round(mean(age)), max_age = max(age))
```

# count is the shortcut

```{r}
# count does the group_by and summarise(n()) in one step.
# Same numbers as above minus the ages. This is what we pivoted last week.
linelist %>%
  count(lhd, sex)
```

# Adding a column per group

```{r}
# summarise gives one row per group. mutate keeps every row but calculates within the group.
# Here each case gets the mean age of its own LHD. Still 50 rows, just one column wider.
# head() only prints the first 6 so the table fits on screen.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd) %>%
  mutate(lhd_mean_age = round(mean(age))) %>%
  head()
```

# Filtering per group

```{r}
# Oldest case in each LHD. Without group_by this would just be the oldest case overall.
# FYI an LHD shows up more than once if cases tie for oldest.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd) %>%
  filter(age == max(age))
```

# Why group? Plots want one row per bar

```{r}
# ggplot needs one row per bar. group_by + summarise is how you get there.
# Last week's plot was counts. This one is mean age.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd) %>%
  summarise(mean_age = mean(age)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_age, y = lhd)) +
  geom_col()
```

# ungroup when done

```{r}
# Grouping sticks to the data until you ungroup. Easy to forget.
# The mutate is just here to stand in for some earlier step. The grouping carries through it.
# So this summarise still runs per LHD. 8 rows instead of 1.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd) %>%
  mutate(lhd_mean_age = mean(age)) %>%
  summarise(cases = n())
```

```{r}
# With ungroup, the same summarise gives one row for the whole data.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd) %>%
  mutate(lhd_mean_age = mean(age)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  summarise(cases = n())
```
